item.title: Version 2.4.1
item.description:
• Arabic is easier to find. In Settings › General, pick Arabic in “Right Option speaks” and Slate sets it up for you: Right Option dictates in Arabic, and Right Option and L together switch it back to English. Before, Arabic only appeared after turning on a second language, which was easy to miss.
  • On macOS 14, the language menus now show Arabic with what it needs, macOS 15 or later, instead of leaving it out, and picking it says where to update macOS.

item.title: Version 2.4.0
item.description:
• A second language on its own talk key. Turn it on in Settings › General and pick any of the languages Slate speaks: French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Polish and 17 more, or Arabic on macOS 15 and later. Hold Right Command to dictate in it, or press Right Option and L together to switch Right Option between your two languages. The island names the language as you speak. Only the language you pick is downloaded, once: about 480 MB for the European languages, 65 MB for Arabic. If you turned on Arabic in 2.3.0, it is already your second language.
  • Right Option can speak another language too. In Settings › General, “Right Option speaks” lists English and the other 24.
  • A shorter setup for new Macs, in five steps. It shows the speech download as it happens, explains each macOS permission before macOS asks for it, lets you try the talk key with each step ticking off as you go, and offers your Mac’s own language at the end.

item.title: Version 2.3.0
item.description:
• Slate is now for sale: a 14-day free trial, then $27 once for one Mac, with a 30-day refund. Everyone who used Slate while it was free keeps it free, with nothing to do. Settings › License says “Founder license”.
  • Arabic dictation. Turn it on in Settings › General, then hold Right Command to dictate in Arabic, or press Right Option and L together to switch Right Option between English and Arabic. The island says which language it is listening in. The Arabic speech files are a one-time download of about 65 MB from slatedictation.com, and they run on this Mac. Arabic needs macOS 15 or later, and is typed without punctuation for now.
  • Fixes. A note started while the last one was still saving could be typed into the app in front instead of kept as a note. Cleaning up a very long take no longer holds Slate up while it works. Slate’s log no longer names the apps you dictate into.
